newsitem.title: USA: CBOT plans electronic trading from members' homes.
newsitem.headline: CBOT plans electronic trading from members' homes.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade expects to start trading from members' homes on its Project A electronic trading system in the third quarter of this year, a CBOT official said Thursday.
Donald Karmazin, CBOT senior vice president, technology, said the expansion was part of its strategy to enhance Project A.
"We are probably going to have the first actual trade occur in the third quarter," Karmazin said at a Futures Industry Association conference here.

"No longer will traders or users of Project A be limited only to the wired connections that exist today either at our La Salle Street building (in Chicago) where we have 50 percent of our terminals or with the other 50 percent which are in the city of Chicago, New York and several others distributed around the country," he said.
Karmazin said the exchange was looking at allowing international access to Project A, and was also in the process of designing a new front end for the system.
He said the third generation of Project A, currently under design, would increase ease of access to users and allow more products to be traded.
"The database management system that Project A has today is somewhat limited," he said. "We're looking forward to a new generation of the system that will give us a lot more capability in that area."
